---
title: "Pipeline"
---

Scripts are numbered in run order. Each writes to `<DATA_ROOT>/data/outputs/` and reads
what the previous step wrote:

```bash
uv run python scripts/20_subsets/21_prepare_input_data.py
```

Most steps take minutes. `31_shap.py` takes about 20 minutes for 208 sites on a
24-thread machine, `41_binagg_per_site.py` about 40.

## Run variants

Every stage from 21 onward carries a `VARIANT` constant. An empty string reads and
writes the baseline paths; any other value inserts a folder level on both sides, so a
variant reads `20_subsets/<VARIANT>/` and writes `30_shap/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/`;
a stage fails on a missing file if its predecessor has not run with the same variant.

| VARIANT | Change | Output through |
|---|---|---|
| empty | none, the published run | every stage |
| `deep-sm` | deepest usable soil water layer per site | stage 49, and the ALE side, 32 and 46 |
| `blocked-cv` | leave-one-year-out instead of a shuffled split | stage 49 |
| `no_ta` | air temperature dropped from the predictors | stage 41 |
| `no_vpd` | VPD dropped from the predictors | stage 31 |
| `mirrored-stages` | stage 44 only, VPD escalates and extreme soil dryness is added last | stage 44 |
| `factorial-cells` | stage 44 only, four soil water classes by four VPD classes, temperature free | stage 44 |

Scripts from 41 onward also take `SITE_SUBSET`, `""` for all sites or `"deeper-only"`
for the 128 sites with a soil water layer below layer 1. Run against the empty variant
and `deep-sm`, the subset gives a matched pair: the same 128 sites at their shallowest
and their deepest layer. Scripts 45, 46, 51, 57 and 66 take no subset.

`31_shap.py` and `32_validate_shap_methods.py` take `SITES` and `MAX_SITES` to limit a
run for timing.

## 10_datasets: site collection

| Script | Function | Writes |
|--------|----------|--------|
| `00_find_overlaps.py` | Lists sites in both AmeriFlux and FLUXNET-SHUTTLE and deletes the AmeriFlux folders; already applied, do not rerun | `10_datasets/` |
| `11_collect_info.py` | One row per dataset found in the five raw sources | `11_datasets_info.csv` |
| `12_create_parquet.py` | Merges the datasets of a site by source priority | `12_parquet_merged/`, `12_datasets_info_parquet.csv` |
| `13_check_available_vars.py` | Which of NEE, LE, GPP, RECO, TA, VPD, SWIN, SWC exist per site, under which name | `13_datasets_info_parquet_vars.csv` |
| `13b_check_available_vars_SWC.py` | Coverage of every soil water layer per site, within the peak months and against layer 1 | `13b_variables_coverage_summary.csv`, `13b_variables_per_site.csv` |
| `14_collect_basic_stats.py` | Record counts, date ranges and basic statistics per variable | `14_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats.csv` |
| `15_remove_sites.py` | Applies the inclusion criteria | `15_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites.csv` |
| `16a` to `16d`, `16_download_era5_mat_map.py` | ERA5 1991 to 2020 normals from Google Earth Engine and the Copernicus CDS | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020*/` |
| `17_add_era5_info.py` | One ERA5 source per site, adds MAT and MAP, logs every decision | `17_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites_era5.csv` |

## 20_subsets: model input

`21_prepare_input_data.py` builds the subset the models see, per site:

1. keep the four months with the highest mean GPP
2. keep measured NEE only (quality flag 0)
3. keep daytime records, `SW_IN_POT > 20`
4. balance the record so every month contributes the same number of years
5. drop records with any missing predictor
6. derive ET from LE and TA, and NEP as `-NEE`
7. z-score every variable within the site

`SWC_LAYER = "shallow"` uses `SWC_F_MDS_1`, `"deepest"` the deepest usable layer per
site, see [Methods](methods.qmd#soil-water-layer). CD-Ygb stores VPD in Pa; the
correction to hPa is applied here. Writes one parquet per site to
`21_subsets_parquet/` and the summary `21_SUBSETS_parquet_vars_stats_subsets.csv`, which
records the soil water layer used per site. `N_WORKERS = 3` by default; the largest sites
need about 3 GB per worker.

`22_data_flow.py` counts the records each filter removes, per site, and checks its final
count against script 21. Of the delivered half-hourly records, 7.1 percent reach the
models; the quality filter removes the most.

## 30_shap: models and attribution

`31_shap.py` fits one XGBoost regressor per site and computes SHAP values. Switches at
the top of the file:

| Switch | Values |
|---|---|
| `FLUX` | `NEP_ZSCORE` (published), `GPP_ZSCORE`, `RECO_ZSCORE`, `ET_ZSCORE`; each writes to its own folder |
| `CV_STRATEGY` | `random` (published, shuffled 5-fold) or `blocked` (leave one year out) |
| `FEATURE_SET` | `full`, `no_vpd`, `no_ta` |
| `TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS` | `False` for the analysis, `True` for the hyperparameter search |

Within each fold, 80 percent of the records are split into 68 percent for fitting and
12 percent for early stopping, and the held-out 20 percent is explained. Every SHAP value
therefore comes from a model that never saw the record. Writes per-site parquet and csv
with predictors, SHAP values and predictions, plus one csv of fold metrics. Unchanged
sites give bit-identical output between runs.

`32_validate_shap_methods.py` fits one model per site on an 85/15 split and computes ALE
curves on 100 grid points per predictor. Writes `{SITE}_ale_curves_{TARGET}.csv`.

## 40_aggregation: results across sites

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `41_binagg_per_site.py` | Bins each site's SHAP values on a two-variable grid with shared edges, for five variable pairs (TA-VPD, SWC-VPD, TA-SWC, ET-VPD, ET-SWC) |
| `42_binagg_across_sites.py` | Averages the site grids, one vote per site |
| `43_binagg_across_igbp.py` | Same, per forest type |
| `44_agg_per_scenario.py` | SHAP means within the stress stages, per site and across sites; `STAGE_SEQUENCE = "published"`, `"mirrored"` or `"factorial"` |
| `45_stage_distributions.py` | Driver medians and quartiles within each stage, in standardized and measured units |
| `46_ale_thresholds.py` | Per-site ALE curves on one grid and their thresholds, overall and per forest type |
| `47_threshold_robustness.py` | Eighteen re-estimations of the VPD threshold with a bootstrap over sites, the 23-setting estimator sweep and leave-one-site-out; feeds Table 1 |
| `48_threshold_exceedance.py` | Share of peak-season daytime half-hours above the threshold, per site and forest type |
| `49_biome_thresholds.py` | One threshold per site, Kruskal-Wallis and Holm-corrected pairwise tests between forest types |

Order: 41, then 42 and 43; 44 any time after 31; 46 after 32; 47 after 46 and after the
`deep-sm`, `deeper-only`, `blocked-cv` and `no_ta` runs have reached stage 41; 49 after
42; 48 after 47 and 49. Bins covered by fewer than half the sites are dropped.

## 50_figures

Figure scripts write to `50_plots/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/<SITE_SUBSET>/`, so a variant
never overwrites a published figure. Scripts 55, 57, 59, 60 and 65 read stage 40 files
(47, 46, 45, 48, 49); scripts 59, 61, 62, 63 and 64 read stage 80 files (89, 87, 81, 82,
86). See [Figures](figures.qmd).

## 80_info: sensitivity checks

Analyses with numbers quoted in the text. They write to
`80_info/<FLUX>/conditional/<VARIANT>/<SITE_SUBSET>/`; where a supplementary table shows
the same numbers, a script of the 50s lays the INFO file out.

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `80_time_scale_coverage.py` | Measured share of a peak-season day, and the records and Stage 8 records left at daily, monthly and yearly resolution |
| `81_threshold_definitions.py` | Peak, steepest decline and zero crossing of the fitted VPD response, with range-edge flags |
| `82_threshold_vs_site_vpd_range.py` | Per-site thresholds by quartile of the site's maximum VPD |
| `83_leave_region_out.py` | Threshold and Stage 8 attribution with Europe, North America or both removed |
| `84_short_record_sensitivity.py` | The same under minimum record lengths |
| `85_wue_vs_vpd.py` | Water use efficiency against VPD per site |
| `86_site_skill.py` | Site-level R2, RMSE, MAE and bias under both cross-validation splits, overall, in Stage 8 and in the high-VPD tail |
| `87_stage_cutoff_percentiles.py` | Empirical share of records below each stage cut-off, against the Gaussian share |
| `88_stage_order_test.py` | Net effect along the published and the mirrored stage order |
| `89_stage_matching.py` | Stage 7 against Stage 8 on matched records |

Scripts 83 and 84 use the median of the per-site thresholds, which sits about 0.07 kPa
below the crossing of the aggregated curve; Table 1 reports the latter.

## 90_deposit: data deposit

The scripts write into `<DATA_ROOT>/deposit_eth_research_collection/`, the files for the
ETH Research Collection. Script 91 also writes the Source Data for the journal into
`<DATA_ROOT>/submission_nature_communications/`. Run 91 and 92 before 93, which lists
their archives in `MANIFEST.csv` and `ARCHIVES.csv`.

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `91_build_source_data.py` | The Source Data: the data file of every figure, table and Supplementary Data file of the main analysis, copied under a plain name (`Fig4_all_sites.csv`, `SupplementaryTable6.xlsx`) with a README; dry run by default, `--build` writes |
| `92_build_demo_data.py` | `ms-forests-vpd_demo.zip`: the model input of one site (CH-Dav) with its published output, so that script 31 can be tried without the full deposit (README, Demo); dry run by default, `--build` writes |
| `93_build_deposit_archives.py` | One uncompressed zip per output stage, with `MANIFEST.csv` and `ARCHIVES.csv`; dry run by default, `--build` writes |
| `94_build_data_flow_chart.py` | `DATA_FLOW.html`, a zoomable chart of every script with the files it reads and writes, drawn from `94_data_flow_graph.json` |

The reads and writes in `94_data_flow_graph.json` were taken from the code by hand. When a
script starts reading or writing a different file, update its entry there and rerun
script 92. Script 94 also writes a copy of the chart to `docs/data_flow.html` for this
site.
